sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, accounting for about 38% of the model's importance, and risk rises sharply as the share of the credit limit in use goes up, especially above roughly 0.7.
Past delinquencies are the second strongest driver, and having at least one delinquency on file raises the predicted risk compared with having none.
Annual income is the third strongest driver, with risk falling as income rises, mostly through the drop between the lowest income band and the middle and upper bands.
Length of credit history has a weak to moderate effect, with longer histories associated with somewhat lower risk, though the data do not settle how large this effect is.

Debt-to-income ratio, number of dependents, months at address, age and recent credit inquiries each have a negligible effect in this model, and the data do not settle whether debt-to-income has any effect at all.
The interactions in the model are small, and the data do not settle whether utilization's effect depends on debt-to-income, so the main drivers can be read largely on their own.
